decisions.reason: Selecting Variation B and tighter kerning does not change the approved Hero V geometry; the source instead reiterates that the accent must copy its right arm.

The client selects Variation B with the already-established common baseline, and the same-message runtime verification already records that successful baseline result without changing its alignment rule.
The source message's hierarchy changes are already represented by a same-message MODIFY that aligns the E/L height to the second V's left arm and preserves its right-arm prominence.
The requested E/L height scaling concerns the separate cap-height requirement, while the kerning selection does not change the E/L construction or architectural design language.
The source changes spacing and surrounding-letter scale but does not alter the second V's copied proportional geometry or construction method.
Requiring the accent to remain a perfect copy of the Hero V right arm does not change the existing rule that their highest points align.
The source message's precise E/L cap-height rule is already represented by a same-message MODIFY, so no additional or augmented Event is needed.
The selection of tighter kerning and common-baseline composition has no effect on the deferred champagne material treatment.
The request to ensure a perfect copy/paste reiterates the existing locked one-to-one derivation rule and does not establish a new value or remove an existing attribute.
The source reiterates the existing Hero-V-to-accent terminal relationship but does not change the terminal treatment, status, or scope.
The composition and kerning decision does not alter the obligation to explain design intentions with review rounds.
